item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00021","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C05","C13","C06"],"selected_candidate_label":"C05","confidence":0.999,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C05 is a nearly verbatim country-substitution template for the child proclamation. It uses the same statutory recital, findings about wartime disruption and reciprocal treatment, operative extension machinery, eligibility dates, deadline, and proclamation closing; the principal substantive adaptation is Luxembourg to Denmark. C13 is likewise an extremely close template, but C05 is later and its wording matches the child slightly more exactly. C06 shares only the generic function of extending a deadline and does not reproduce the trademark-specific language or machinery.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"Whereas by the act of Congress approved July 17, 1946, 60 Stat. 568, the President is authorized...to grant an extension of time...for the renewal of trade-mark registrations...","parent_excerpt":"Whereas by the act of Congress approved July 17, 1946, 60 Stat. 568, the President is authorized...to grant an extension of time...for the renewal of trade-mark registrations...","explanation":"The statutory authority recital is essentially identical."},{"child_excerpt":"with respect to trade-marks of nationals of Denmark registered in the United States Patent Office which have been subject to renewal on or after September 3, 1939...because of conditions growing out of World War II, such disruption or suspension of facilities...","parent_excerpt":"with respect to trade-marks of nationals of Luxembourg registered in the United States Patent Office which have been subject to renewal on or after September 3, 1939...because of conditions growing out of World War II, such disruption or suspension of facilities...","explanation":"The same factual finding is reused with only the country changed."},{"child_excerpt":"Denmark accords substantially equal treatment...and...the time...is hereby extended with respect to such registrations which expired after September 3, 1939, and before June 30, 1947, until and including June 30, 1948.","parent_excerpt":"Luxembourg accords substantially equal treatment...and...the time...is hereby extended with respect to such registrations which expired after September 3, 1939, and before June 30, 1947, until and including June 30, 1948.","explanation":"The reciprocal-treatment finding and complete operative extension provision—including all dates—are materially identical."}]}
